title: Completeness
summary: Completeness can mean that every semantic consequence is provable, or that a space has no missing limits; the meanings must be named.

content.plain: Completeness can mean that every semantic consequence is provable, or that a space has no missing limits; the meanings must be named.
content.exact: Logical completeness for a proof system S and semantics ⊨ means: if Γ⊨P, then Γ⊢ₛP. Other branches use different completeness predicates.
content.example: Gödel's completeness theorem concerns first-order logical consequence, not the completeness of every arithmetical theory.
content.caveat: Do not confuse logical completeness, theory completeness, metric completeness, and Gödel incompleteness.
